correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the idempotent-transposition condition to a corner pRp: symmetry makes p central and forces the transposed product into the corner, reversibility makes the corner directly finite, and the abelian unit group then forces equality of the two triple products. The reverse unit-group implication follows from a triple product equal to 1.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Symmetric subsets and I-symmetric rings are prior art, and the 2022 I-symmetric paper contains a closely related abelian-semiperfect special case. Its full body was not inspected, so possible hidden coverage of the unrestricted unit-group criterion is explicitly retained as the principal risk. No prior statement identifying the 2026 pro-symmetric notion with I-symmetry was located.

value.rationale: The criterion identifies a newly introduced projection-based class with an existing idempotent-symmetry class, removes the involution from the classification, and yields immediate sharp consequences for clean rings and division rings.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
